issues.title: Policy edits prevent terminal purchase snapshots from revoking existing access
issues.proof: Refund, suspension and expiry snapshots all reach manual review after 12 accelerated fixture retries; prior entitlement remains active and fresh online Go SDK activation executes export. The expiry snapshot has a deadline in the past.

issues.title: Lower-plan synchronization blocked by occupied device count retains higher-plan authorization
issues.proof: With two active devices, one-device basic snapshot stays unapplied through 12 retries; fresh online Go SDK on an existing host still executes pro.

issues.title: Ordinary renewal clears a manual per-license device limit
issues.proof: Manual limit one blocks a second device; ordinary renewal resets limit to policy value two, and another host activates using the actual SDK.

issues.owner: Launch Go SDK; optional Launch server logout-only capability
issues.title: Failed account logout loses retry state and a subsequent logout reports success without revoking the old session
issues.proof: Actual Launch HTTP service and Go account SDK with a licensing runtime double: first account logout fails in transport; local runtime and account record are cleared; after transport recovers, second Logout returns nil without any accepted logout request. The original token authenticates and fetches a new signed assertion through the real identity HTTP endpoint.

Local runtime was stopped; this probe does not claim local feature execution after logout.

limitations: No payments were charged or refunded with a real provider. The first three probes submit exact purchase snapshots through the real Licentivo API and worker, using its real MySQL and official Go SDK; they are not a complete PSP-to-Launch-to-Licentivo deployment test.
Backoff is accelerated by changing only the selected event availability time in the dedicated fixture, without altering business implementation or its outcomes.
Launch logout test uses a licensing runtime double and proves a live server session and new identity, not local protected execution after logout or a single end-to-end stolen-token activation.
Only Go SDK behavior is dynamically established for these findings; no claim that all nine language SDKs were tested.

An initial downgrade probe accidentally treated a configured device ID as overrideable; official Go SDK correctly derives host identity. The final probe first binds that actual host and then tests it again. Initial log retained privately.
